clue.text: Landscape gardener's fortunate, heading off for Derby area

parts.note: William Kent was an 18th-century English landscape gardener; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: heading off says the word for fortunate loses its first letter

parts.note: fortunate means lucky

explanation.surface: A garden designer has a lucky break and sets off for the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' strips the L from LUCKY to leave UCKY. The Kentucky Derby is America's most famous horse race, run at Louisville.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kentucky Derby is run in that US state, so the state is the area of that famous race.

clue.text: Rubbish I weep over in entrances to King's Head

indicators.note: in says the I and turned weeping word sit inside the two opening letters
entrances to means the opening letters of the two following words
over says the weeping word is turned backwards

parts.note: to sob is to weep

explanation.surface: A tearful complaint of nonsense at the doors of a pub called the King's Head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the weeping word backwards, and 'in' sets it with I inside the King's Head initials. The King's Head is a common British pub name, which gives the surface its picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Kibosh is old slang for nonsense or rubbish, as well as in the phrase put the kibosh on.

clue.text: Noble accepted in city? All but

indicators.note: accepted in says the noble is taken inside the city's letters

parts.note: NY is New York City
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: Is a noble welcomed in the city? Almost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted in' puts EARL between N and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly means almost, all but, as in all but finished.

clue.text: Endless stress beginning to grip lackey

indicators.note: Endless means the stress word loses its last letter

parts.note: to underline is to stress or emphasise

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of grip

explanation.surface: Constant strain begins to grip a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the E from UNDERLINE; 'beginning to' adds G from grip.
explanation.definitionFit: An underling is a subordinate, someone of low rank like a lackey.

clue.text: Remain calm, unlike Catherine Howard

definitions.meaning: to stay composed in a crisis
Henry VIII's fifth wife Catherine Howard was beheaded in 1542, so she did not keep it

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: Catherine Howard, fifth wife of Henry VIII, was executed by beheading.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep one's head is an idiom for staying composed in a crisis.

clue.text: It takes a day to go round hunting on this

parts.note: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: to go round says the day's abbreviation wraps itself about the single letter

parts.note: Fri is the short form of Friday

explanation.surface: Something that needs a whole day to travel round, used for hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' puts A inside FRI to make FARI, after SA. 'It' as SA (sex appeal) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition to hunt or watch big game, so one goes hunting on it.

clue.text: Lessen a cricketer's energy

parts.note: a bat is a batsman, a cricketer; the 's is a link
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A cricket player loses some of his energy.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'bat' is a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to diminish or lessen in force.

clue.text: Rook captured by a seasoned keeper

indicators.note: captured by says the rook letter is held inside the other pieces

parts.note: seasoned means matured or mature
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: In chess, a rook is taken by an experienced player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured by' puts R between A and MATURE. A magnet's keeper is a soft iron bar laid across its poles, also called an armature.
explanation.definitionFit: An armature is the iron bar placed across a magnet's poles, technically called its keeper.

clue.text: Oblique remark from local union leader in Parisian function

parts.note: a local is a British pub, an inn

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of union

parts.note: en is French for in
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: A remark from the pub's union boss at a Paris event.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for one's nearby pub; 'union leader' gives U, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect hint or insinuation, an oblique remark.

clue.text: Latest directions accompanying Norwegian drama

parts.note: Brand is a verse drama by the Norwegian playwright Henrik Ibsen
N, E and W are compass points, three directions

explanation.surface: The newest stage instructions come with a play from Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Directions' looks like stage directions, but it is three compass points; the answer's pieces come in the reverse of the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brand-new is completely new, the latest thing to appear.

clue.text: Servant guarding male doctor's coveted riches

indicators.note: guarding says the servant word stands round the other pieces, protecting them

parts.note: a manservant is a man, so servant gives man
MO is a medical officer, a doctor; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A servant protects a male doctor's sought-after wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guarding' reads like a bodyguard's job in the surface, but it is the container signal. Mammon is the biblical personification of wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammon is wealth regarded as an object of greedy devotion, riches people covet.

clue.text: Black Maria a force ordered new

indicators.note: ordered says these letters are arranged into a new sequence

parts.note: the letters of Maria
taken as written
the letters of force

explanation.surface: A police van was told to be new.
explanation.walkthrough: A Black Maria is British slang for a police van, so the surface hides the definition inside a familiar phrase; 'ordered' is the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Afro-American describes a black American of African descent, so black is the adjective.

clue.text: Sort of power line in wing

indicators.note: in says the line's letter goes inside the word for wing

parts.note: to wing is to fly, to soar

explanation.surface: A kind of power cable runs within an aircraft wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wing' looks like a noun but is the verb, to fly high.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar power is energy taken from the sun, so solar is one sort of power.

clue.text: Slightly eccentric, putting money on cricket side first

indicators.note: first says the cricket side goes before the money pieces

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field, opposite the leg side
a cent is a small coin, some money
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone a bit odd bets money on one side of a cricket field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting money on' reads as betting, but on gives RE (concerning). In cricket the off side is one half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-centre means not quite in the middle, figuratively a little odd or unconventional.

clue.text: Long established in home, freely travelled around

indicators.note: around says the travel word goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: to tour is to travel, so travelled gives toured

indicators.note: freely says the letters move about loosely into a new order

parts.note: the letters of in home

explanation.surface: Settled at home, someone has roamed widely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' is the anagram signal for the two words before it, and 'around' wraps the travel word round the result, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Time-honoured means respected because of long tradition, established over a long period.

clue.text: Go past old minister standing up before open fire

indicators.note: standing up in a down clue says the minister's letters read upwards

parts.note: Rev, reverend, is a minister of religion
to open fire is to shoot

explanation.surface: A retired clergyman stands up before a fire is lit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' turns REV into VER in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshoot is to go beyond a target or stopping point.

clue.text: Lapsed badly, pinching house plant

indicators.note: pinching says the jumbled letters grab the house letters inside them
badly says the letters of lapsed are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone who has lapsed into bad ways steals a house plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lapsed badly' reads as moral failure, but 'badly' is the anagram signal; 'pinching' reads as theft, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-family plant, in legend the flower of the Greek underworld.

clue.text: Like some salts Aggie's on for a change

indicators.note: for a change says these letters swap places into something new

parts.note: the letters of Aggie's on

explanation.surface: Aggie puts on some salts for variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salts' suggests chemistry or bath salts, but an old salt is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt is an experienced sailor, so seagoing describes sea-faring ones.

clue.text: Tool con man used to enclose shelf

indicators.note: used to enclose says the con man word wraps round the shelf word

parts.note: a shammer is someone who shams, a fraud or con man
a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: A swindler uses a tool to box in a shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'con man' looks like a swindler using the tool, but it is the container word; 'used to enclose' wraps it round the shelf, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledgehammer is a heavy long-handled hammer, a tool for breaking stone.

clue.text: Fellow introduces literary gossip? There's no hurry

parts.note: a fellow is a man
ana is a collection of anecdotes or gossip about a writer

explanation.surface: A man brings in some bookish chat, saying there's plenty of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ana' is a crossword-favourite word for literary anecdotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Manana, Spanish for tomorrow, is used to say something can be put off indefinitely.

clue.text: Some hire me, dying for a cure

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A desperate plea: employ me, I'm dying for a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for a cure' as the definition, but only 'cure' can stand in for the answer; 'for a' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a treatment that cures, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Position of senior academic, one supporting young scoffers?

definitions.meaning: a senior professorship, a professor's chair being their post
a child's tall feeding seat holds up small children as they scoff their food

explanation.walkthrough: Scoffers here are eaters, not mockers; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A highchair is a raised seat for feeding infants, and a high chair is also an exalted academic post.

clue.text: Dish that's served after chop

indicators.note: served after says the that's letters come after the chop word

parts.note: to chop is to cut
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A dish comes out after the meat chop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' reads as food, but it is slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is slang for an attractive person, just like a cutie.

clue.text: Mount horse-drawn vehicle

definitions.meaning: to mount a play is to put it on

explanation.surface: Climb aboard a carriage pulled by horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' suggests climbing on a horse, but here it is putting on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage a show is to mount it, and a stage was a stagecoach running between stops.

clue.text: Petite daughter isn't commonly 27, ultimately

parts.note: ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the answer to clue 27

explanation.surface: A small daughter is not, in common speech, wobbly in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 refers to the answer of 27 across, whose last letter is Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Dainty means delicately small and pretty, which is close to petite.

clue.text: Honour officer infiltrating a rebel environment

indicators.note: infiltrating says the officer gets inside the rebel's name

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450
Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an officer

explanation.surface: An officer is decorated for getting inside a rebel's surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infiltrating' puts COL into CADE; 'environment' just underlines that CADE surrounds it. Jack Cade is the English rebel of 1450.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or mark of praise, an honour bestowed on someone.

clue.text: I fell, knocking over chap with register

parts.note: a log is a register or record

indicators.note: knocking over says the name is turned backwards

parts.note: Reg is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: Someone falls, upending a man who has a register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking over' turns REG into GER. 'I fell' reads as a stumble, but it is what a tree-feller says.
explanation.definitionFit: A logger fells trees, so the clue speaks in the voice of a lumberjack.

clue.text: In France, a date that's not firmly fixed

parts.note: un is French for a
a steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend, a date

explanation.surface: In France, a date arrangement remains provisional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'date' looks like a calendar day, but it is a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsteady is wobbly, not securely fixed in place.
